Name: Lincoln Douglas Square
Description: The site of the final Lincoln-Douglas debate in 1858

Name: Lyman Trumbull House
Description: The home of former Senator Lyman Trumbull, who helped construct the 13th Amendment

Name: Riverview Park
Description: A park overlooking the Mississippi River with walking paths, benches, and great views.

Name: Olin Park
Description: A local park that has a playground and a large, open field.

Name: Rock Spring Park
Description: A large park in Alton with wooded areas and walking trails.

Name: McPike Mansion
Description: A historic mansion built in 1869 that's known for its architecture and ghost stories.

Name: College Avenue Presbyterian Church
Description: A historic church that has been part of Alton's community since the 1800s.

Name: Godfrey Gilman & Co. Warehouse
Description: A former warehouse connected to Elijah Lovejoy and Alton's abolitionist history.

Name: Hayner Public Library
Description: A community library in alton providing access to local history archives and digital resources.

Name: Lovejoy State Memorial
Description: A monument honoring Elijah P. Lovejoy, an abolitionist who was killed defending his printing press in 1837.

Name: Alton Military Prison
Description: The site of a Civil War prison that held Confederate prisoners during the 1860s.

Name: Post Commons
Description: A former post office that has been turned into a café and community gathering space.

Name: Alton City Hall
Description: The building where Alton's city government operates and serves its residents.

Name: Old Bakery Beer Company
Description: A brewery and restaurant inside a former bakery building in downtown Alton.

Name: Miles Davis Statue
Description: A statue honoring Miles Davis, the famous jazz musician who was born in Alton in 1926.

Name: SIUE School of Dental Medicine
Description: A dental school in Alton that provides education for future dentists and dental care for the community.

Name: Chain of Rocks Park
Description: A park near the Mississippi River known for its outdoor recreation areas and nearby historic Chain of Rocks Bridge.

Name: Alton Riverfront Green Space
Description: A public area along the Mississippi River with walking paths and places to enjoy the waterfront.

Name: National Great Rivers Museum
Description: A museum that provides guided tours teaching visitors about the Mississippi River's history, wildlife, and how river navigation works.
